gaps.title: AG-UI client for the scaffolded React app

candidates.name: @ag-ui/client
candidates.rationale: Maintenance signal is strong: pushed yesterday, 74 releases, latest published the same day as this analysis. It supplies the RunAgentInput Zod schema, AbortController-based run cancellation, and untruncate-json for partial-frame recovery — all things a hand-rolled client would have to reinvent badly.
risks: Pre-1.0 (0.0.59). No semver stability guarantee; breaking changes may land in patch releases.
Pulls rxjs 7.8.1 and protobuf tooling into every scaffolded app, whether or not the app streams.
@types/uuid appears as a runtime dependency rather than a devDependency — a packaging smell worth watching.

candidates.name: hand-rolled EventSource client
candidates.rationale: EventSource cannot POST, and the AG-UI transport requires POSTing a RunAgentInput body with Accept: text/event-stream. A hand-rolled client would need fetch + ReadableStream + manual frame parsing, plus reimplementation of partial-JSON recovery. The assessment's '~10 lines' estimate covered only frame formatting, not the client.

candidates.name: @copilotkit/react-core
candidates.rationale: The reference AG-UI frontend, healthy (published 2026-08-27) and far more mature at 1.69.3. But it is a full agent-UI framework with opinionated components, which conflicts with this repo's own scaffolder conventions and state architecture. Revisit only if the phase goal expands from transport to full chat UI.

candidates.name: @ag-ui/encoder (server-side, Node route)
candidates.rationale: EventEncoder.encodeSSE is literally `data: ${JSON.stringify(event)}\n\n` and getContentType() handles negotiation. Trivial to adopt if the surface lives in Node, and it keeps encoding aligned with upstream.

candidates.name: Axum SSE route in scaffold-react-vite-axum.sh
candidates.rationale: The scaffolder exists (431 lines) but has NO SSE precedent — grep for sse/event-stream/stream found only asset-serving and SPA-fallback code. Everything would be net-new Rust.
risks: No existing streaming code to extend
Splits the event-type source of truth across TS and Rust

candidates.name: ag-ui-rs / ag-ui / tirea-protocol-ag-ui (crates.io)
candidates.rationale: All effectively unused. Download counts in the tens-to-hundreds indicate no production adoption and no maintenance guarantee. Depending on one would be a larger risk than writing the ~40 lines of SSE framing directly.

candidates.name: Extend openai-proxy (original plan of record)
candidates.rationale: Three independent reasons. (1) Out of repo — phase-1b's scope_note states 'No openai-proxy vendoring'; a phase that must modify a codebase this repo does not contain cannot verify its own acceptance criteria. (2) Nothing to extend — all four AG-UI endpoint candidates 404 (assess F-1), so this is net-new work wherever it lands. (3) Wrong coupling — every scaffolded app would depend on a separately-deployed proxy at localhost:8181, making generated output non-self-contained.
candidates.note: openai-proxy remains correct for inference routing; it is the wrong home for a protocol surface the scaffolded app must own.
candidates.source: plan.md:65 named this as the plan of record; evaluated and rejected on evidence.

gaps.title: Event-kind enum drift
gaps.severity_upgraded: Assess rated this WARNING with 2 missing kinds. The shipped tarball shows 10 missing kinds AND one incorrect name. Upgraded to BLOCKING.

wrong_name.impact: A protocol-conformant AG-UI spec using TOOL_CALL_ARGS is REJECTED by our validator today. This is a live correctness defect in shipped code, not a forward-looking gap.

gaps.title: scaffold-react-vite-agui.sh does not exist
gaps.rationale: No external candidate applies. T1 search for generic Vite/React scaffold generators returned nothing usable, and adopting a third-party generator would discard this repo's established conventions (brand-TOML injection, kebab-case rename pass, import-rewrite, architectural ESLint config). The correct model is the in-repo precedent, not an external tool.

candidates.name: in-repo scaffolder pattern

evidence.scaffold-react-vite-tauri.sh: 230 lines — thin wrapper over the base, closest size analogue

candidates.rationale: scaffold-react-vite-tauri.sh (230 lines) is the closest analogue: a thin wrapper that layers one concern onto the base scaffolder. An AG-UI variant should follow that shape rather than forking the 1160-line base.

open_questions_resolved.question: Adopt @ag-ui/* or hand-roll?
open_questions_resolved.answer: Adopt @ag-ui/client for the client; adopt @ag-ui/encoder only if the server is Node. The hand-roll option was rejected on a concrete technical ground the assessment missed: EventSource cannot POST.

open_questions_resolved.question: Where does the server surface live?
open_questions_resolved.answer: Node route. All three candidate homes evaluated: openai-proxy REJECTED (out of repo, nothing to extend, non-self-contained output), Axum REJECTED (no SSE precedent, no viable Rust crate), Node RECOMMENDED (reuses @ag-ui/encoder so the event contract has one source of truth).

open_questions_resolved.question: Pin @ag-ui/* exactly or use a caret range?
open_questions_resolved.answer: Pin exact (0.0.59). Pre-1.0 packages may ship breaking changes in a patch bump. Plan implements and records the pins; the decision itself is closed.

open_questions_remaining: Mock agent vs real LLM backing — unchanged from assess; a scope decision, not a research question.
Store reduction semantics for streamed events — a design question for plan. @ag-ui/client's rxjs Observable shape constrains it, since events arrive as a stream rather than callbacks.
